frame_metadata.gps_note: First take with GPS on every frame. App frames carry a 9-key GPS block written by the F0 build; stock-camera HEICs carry Apple's full 15-key block. Both bind the frame to the Met to within a few metres.

source_note: App frames are camera-roll copies (Image Capture over USB) bound to the manifest by capture time with tools/manifest/bind-frames.py — see derived/2026-09-20-met-frames.json.

expected.date_edtf_note: BCE years are astronomical: 375 BCE is -0374. Ranges are intervals; '~' marks each end when the label says 'ca.'. A named span like 'late 6th century' is written as the conventional interval and noted in date_raw.

differ.title: label 'with a lid', API 'with lid'
differ.attribution_field: The API carries the qualifier in a separate field, artistPrefix='Attributed to the', with artistRole='Artist'. A consumer reading artistDisplayName alone gets 'Cesnola Painter' as bare authorship — the API's own structure is the laundering risk §4.6 warns about.

traps.three_candidates: On-device: ['750-740', '74.51.965', '7451.965']. The machine offered the date first; the human picked the second. The third is the real number with a period dropped, which is the D14 class of failure — a corrupted key at high confidence. Mac OCR of the same frame returned only '7451.965'.
traps.donation_year_disagrees_with_prefix: '1874–76' — the one label of fourteen where the credit-line year is a range. The agreement heuristic (year ↔ first component) still works on the first year.
traps.second_qualifier_in_corpus: After 'Attributed to' on the Dawkins print (mcny-38.447.4). Same vocabulary, different institution, different century — the qualifier survives on the label in both and must survive in the graph.
